crosswalk: Seed-First AI Act (draft v2) <-> UN and international instruments
external_instrument: UN High-level Advisory Body on AI, 'Governing AI for Humanity' (final report, 2024); Global Digital Compact (2024); UNGA resolution 78/265 (2024); UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021); UNDRIP (2007); UNCRC General Comment No. 25 (2021); Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225, 2024)
status: Informational mapping for policy analysis. Not legal advice. Entries with verify=true need confirmation against primary sources.

relationship_vocabulary.aligned: Same objective and broadly equivalent commitment.
relationship_vocabulary.seed_first_extends: Seed-First covers the commitment and extends its scope.
relationship_vocabulary.partial: Overlapping but narrower or differently framed.
relationship_vocabulary.analogous: Different mechanism serving a comparable function.

entries.notes: A scientific panel could supply the evidence base for Tier 1 Resource Budget methodologies.

entries.external_instrument: HLAB-AI final report; Global Digital Compact
entries.notes: A global dialogue offers a venue for mutual recognition of national ICT decisions.
The machine-readable policy schema is a candidate interoperable standard.

entries.external_provision: Recommendations 4 and 5 (capacity development network; global fund for AI)
entries.notes: The Global South Epistemic Protection Fund and AU capacity provisions pursue the same capacity and financing goals, with an added emphasis on community governance and language resources.
Seed-First specifies collective data rights: cognitive sovereignty, FPIC and CARE.

entries.external_provision: Recommendation 7 (AI office within the UN Secretariat)
entries.notes: v2 prefers building on existing UN coordination over a new stand-alone High Commission.

entries.external_provision: Safe, secure and trustworthy AI for sustainable development
entries.notes: Shared framing of AI as serving sustainable development.

entries.external_instrument: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
entries.external_provision: Values (incl. environment and ecosystem flourishing); policy areas on environment, gender, data policy
entries.notes: UNESCO sets non-binding values and policy actions. Seed-First converts several of them into hard constraints.
Participation in decision-making, free, prior and informed consent, and control over traditional knowledge.

entries.external_provision: Children's rights in the digital environment
entries.notes: Best interests of the child, protection from economic exploitation and harmful content, and data protection in digital services.

entries.external_instrument: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225)
entries.external_provision: Remedies, procedural safeguards, relationship with other human-rights protections
entries.notes: Both instruments require accessible remedies and preserve stronger existing protections.
No international instrument sets binding resource budgets for AI systems.
